packageRules.description: k3s tags are vX.Y.Z+k3sN, and the +k3sN build is a real release (v1.33.13+k3s2). Applies to every k3s-io/k3s pin (the SUC Plans and a committed k3s_version tfvars, see the customManagers). No matchUpdateTypes: versioning is decided before the update type is known. separateMinorPatch: k3s ships a patch for every supported minor on the same day, and with one branch a waiting minor PR would absorb the patch for the running minor. separateMultipleMinor: a new minor (v1.38.0, skipped below) must not hide an eligible older one (v1.37.3). The k3s group keeps the Plans and the tfvars in one PR, outside the preset's weekly maintenance group.

k3s minors are taken only from their third patch (x.y.3), once the first rounds of regressions are fixed. A minor update whose new version is x.y.0-x.y.2 opens no PR; the next eligible patch does. Patches are untouched: they follow the preset (7-day gate, automerge).
k3s minors from x.y.3 automerge after the preset's 14-day minor gate. system-upgrade-controller applies the new Plans in its next window (gitops/system-upgrade/plans.yaml), one node at a time.
prBodyNotes: k3s minor from its x.y.3 release: it automerges once CI passes and system-upgrade-controller applies it in the next upgrade window. Check the release notes for removed APIs while it waits.

packageRules.description: k3s majors upgrade the cluster through system-upgrade-controller as soon as they merge: a person reviews them.
prBodyNotes: **Why this waits for you:** a k3s major upgrades the cluster through system-upgrade-controller in its next window, one node at a time. Read the release notes for removed APIs first.

packageRules.description: OS releases (vars.tf ubuntu_version / opensuse_leap_version, and the import script's LEAP_VERSION): Ubuntu from endoflife.date, openSUSE Leap from openSUSE's own release API (custom.opensuse-leap). They change what nodes created afterwards boot; running nodes are never replaced on an image change (compute.tf ignore_changes). feat(os): so auto-release cuts a release that names the new OS instead of folding it into chore(deps).

Ubuntu: endoflife.date reports a cycle's latest point release (26.04.1) once there is one, and the bare cycle (26.04) before. extractVersion keeps only LTS cycles (xx.04 of an even year, never interim releases) that already have a point release and writes them back as xx.04, the value OCI's operating_system_version uses. So a new LTS is proposed from its .1 point release (when Ubuntu itself opens LTS-to-LTS upgrades); minimumReleaseAge 90 days is the backstop. Point releases of the current LTS normalise to the same xx.04 and open no PR. The required Plan check runs the image lookup's postcondition against the live tenancy, so a release OCI does not publish yet fails the PR instead of merging.
prBodyNotes: New Ubuntu LTS: only nodes created after this merges boot it (rebuilds, pool replacements); running nodes keep their OS. The Plan check confirmed OCI publishes an aarch64 image for it, not that cloud-init succeeds on it: test a rebuild before relying on it.

packageRules.description: openSUSE Leap, from get.opensuse.org's distributions API (custom.opensuse-leap): endoflife.date added Leap releases weeks late (16.1 was missing while openSUSE already called it Stable). The datasource keeps releases in state Stable or EOL, so Beta and RC builds never match. The API has no release dates, so timestamp-optional: with the default timestamp-required the preset's 14-day minor gate would hold a dateless update forever; openSUSE's Stable state is the gate instead. The image is a custom import, so the bump cannot reach nodes by itself: after it merges, new nodes keep booting the newest imported image and plans warn (checks.tf) until the new release is imported, then pick it up without os_image_id. The group keeps vars.tf and the import script in one PR, outside the preset's weekly maintenance group. allowedVersions drops the legacy 42.x numbering (Leap 42.1-42.3, 2015-2017), which sorts above 16.0.
prBodyNotes: New openSUSE Leap release: run `scripts/import-opensuse-aarch64.sh` (now defaulting to the new release) after merging. Until then new nodes boot the newest image already imported and plans warn; afterwards the module resolves the new image by itself (unless you pin `os_image_id`). Running nodes are never replaced.

opensuse-leap.description: openSUSE Leap releases from openSUSE's distributions API (also behind get.opensuse.org), released ones only: state Stable or EOL.

customManagers.description: openSUSE Leap release imported by scripts/import-opensuse-aarch64.sh (LEAP_VERSION, renovate comment on the line above). Same depName as opensuse_leap_version in vars.tf, so a bump updates both in one PR.

k3s pinned in the system-upgrade-controller Plans: the inline renovate comment sits directly above the version: line (gitops/system-upgrade/plans.yaml shows how). Commented-out lines don't match, so the default channel-based Plans have no pin.

k3s_version pinned in a committed *.auto.tfvars (e.g. example/k3s-version.auto.tfvars; terraform.tfvars itself holds secrets and is gitignored), with the renovate comment on the line above. Same depName as the Plans, so a bump updates both in one PR.
Update versions declared with inline renovate comments in vars.tf
Update Helm chart versions declared with inline renovate comments in gitops YAML files
Update external-dns chart version hardcoded in create_external_dns_app() shell function. Must be kept in sync with gitops/optional/external-dns.yaml targetRevision.
Update container image tags referenced with inline renovate comments in gitops YAML files (e.g. curlimages/curl in gitops/node-cordon-alert).
